questions.question: The average of 15 results is 52. If the average of first 8 results is 56 and that of the last 8 results is 55, then what will be the value of 8th result?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of 15 results = 52

The average of first 8 results = 56

The average of last 8 results = 55

**Formula used:**

The sum of N numbers = average of N number × N

**Calculation:**

Sum of 15 results = 52 × 15 = 780

Sum of the first 8 results = 56 × 8 = 448

Sum of the last 8 results = 55 × 8 = 440

The value of 8th result = (Sum of the first 8 results + Sum of the last 8 results) - Sum of 15 results

⇒ (448 + 440) - 780

⇒ 888 - 780 = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

questions.question: Profit obtained on selling an article for Rs. 600 is equal to the loss incurred on selling the same article for Rs. 400. If selling price is Rs. 750, then what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit on selling an article for Rs.600 = the loss on selling the same article for Rs.400

**Formula used:**

Loss = cost price (C.P) - selling price (S.P)

Profit = selling price (S.P) - cost price (C.P)

Profit % = {(S.P - C.P) × 100}/C.P

**Calculation:**

According to the question:

⇒ 600 - C.P = C.P - 400

⇒ 2 × C.P = 1000

⇒ C.P = Rs.500

New S.P = Rs.750

Profit % = {(S.P - C.P) × 100}/C.P

⇒ {(750 - 500) × 100}/500

⇒ {250 × 100}/500 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

Total work = efficiency × total time

Time taken by A : Time taken by B = 1 : 2

⇒ 1 unit = 20 days

Time taken by A = 20 days

Total work = 20 × 2 = 40 units

Required time to work together = 40/3

**∴ The correct answer is (40/3).**

questions.question: An alloy contains copper, zinc, and nickel in the ratio of 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 5 respectively. What quantity of nickel (in kg) must be added to 100 kg of this alloy to have the new ratio of copper, zinc and nickel 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 6 respectively?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total initial ratio parts = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10 units.

10 units = 100 kg ⇒ 1 unit = 10 kg.

Since the ratio parts for Copper and Zinc (3 : 2) remain unchanged in the new ratio, we can directly compare the Nickel units.

Increase in Nickel ratio units = New parts − Old parts = 6 − 5 = 1 unit.

Quantity of Nickel added = 1 unit × 10 kg = 10 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial weight of the alloy = 100 kg

Initial ratio of Copper : Zinc : Nickel = 3 : 2 : 5

New ratio of Copper : Zinc : Nickel = 3 : 2 : 6

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22519f05f7504b63ab8b9d9383b0c3bd2c5c2769ed4536d3e28a07aafa33b3e9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total initial parts = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10 parts

⇒ 10 parts = 100 kg

⇒ 1 part = 100 ÷ 10 = 10 kg

⇒ Initial Copper = 3 × 10 = 30 kg

⇒ Initial Zinc = 2 × 10 = 20 kg

⇒ Initial Nickel = 5 × 10 = 50 kg

Let the quantity of Nickel added be x kg.

⇒ New Nickel quantity = (50 + x) kg

The new ratio of Copper to Nickel in the alloy is 3 : 6.

⇒ Copper ÷ New Nickel = 3 ÷ 6

⇒ 30 ÷ (50 + x) = 1 ÷ 2

⇒ 50 + x = 30 × 2

⇒ 50 + x = 60

⇒ x = 10 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 10 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Component Principle

When only one component is added or removed from an alloy, the quantities of all other components remain unchanged. Their ratio parts can be directly compared if made equal.

Balancing Ratios

If the unchanging components have different ratio parts in the initial and final states, find their LCM to equalize them before analyzing the changing component's parts.

Replacement Concept

If a fraction of the mixture is replaced by a single element, calculate the remaining mixture's base quantities first, and then add the new replaced value to the target component.

If Mohan travels with 60 percent speed of his usual speed, then he will reach 10 minutes late. What is the usual time taken by him?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New speed = 60% = 3/5 of usual speed.

If speed becomes a/b of usual speed, Usual Time = [a / (b − a)] × Late Time

Here, a = 3, b = 5, Late Time = 10 minutes.

Usual Time = [3 / (5 − 3)] × 10

Usual Time = (3 / 2) × 10 = 15 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Let the usual speed be S and usual time be T minutes.

Distance remains constant in both cases. Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9e16a9d605a261afbc789391f4de3166542704330c1ae25742d7437bdf832c6.png] 

⇒ Usual Distance = S × T

⇒ New Speed = 60% of S = 0.6S

⇒ New Time = (T + 10) minutes

⇒ New Distance = 0.6S × (T + 10)

Equating both distances:

⇒ S × T = 0.6S × (T + 10)

⇒ T = 0.6T + 6

⇒ T − 0.6T = 6

⇒ 0.4T = 6

⇒ T = 6 ÷ 0.4 = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T). Therefore, Speed Ratio = Inverse of Time Ratio.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2ab) ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |a − b|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = a + b.

questions.question:
After interchanging which two signs, the value of the given equation will be '11'?

32 + 3 - 12 ÷ 18 × 9
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png] 

Option 1) : + and -

Given equation is : 32 + 3 - 12 ÷ 18 × 9 = 11

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 32 - 3 + 12 ÷ 18 × 9 = 11

⇒ 32 - 3 + __**12 ÷ 18**__ × 9 = 11

⇒ 32 - 3 + __**0.66 × 9**__ = 11

⇒ __**32**__ - 3 __**+ 6**__ = 11

⇒ __**38 - 3**__ = 11

⇒ 35 ≠ 11

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : × and -

Given equation is : 32 + 3 - 12 ÷ 18 × 9 = 11

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 32 + 3 × 12 ÷ 18 - 9 = 11

⇒ 32 + 3 × __**12 ÷ 18**__ - 9 = 11

⇒ 32 + __**3 × 0.66**__ - 9 = 11

⇒ __**32 + 2**__ - 9 = 11

⇒ __**34 - 9**__ = 11

⇒ 25 ≠ 11

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : ÷ and -

Given equation is : 32 + 3 - 12 ÷ 18 × 9 = 11

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 32 + 3 ÷ 12 - 18 × 9 = 11

⇒ 32 + __**3 ÷ 12**__ - 18 × 9 = 11

⇒ 32 + 0.25 - __**18 × 9**__ = 11

⇒ __**32 + 0.25**__ - 162 = 11

⇒ 32.25 - 162 = 11

⇒ -129.75 ≠ 11

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : ÷ and × 

Given equation is : 32 + 3 - 12 ÷ 18 × 9 = 11

After interchanging the two signs the equation is as follows : 32 + 3 - 12 × 18 ÷ 9 = 11

⇒ 32 + 3 - 12 × __**18 ÷ 9**__ = 11

⇒ 32 + 3 - __**12 × 2**__ = 11

⇒ __**32 + 3**__ - 24 = 11

⇒ __**35 - 24**__ = 11

⇒ **11 = 11**

**LHS = RHS**

Hence, the correct answer is **"÷ and ×".**

• **The materials, through which things can be seen, are called transparent materials.**
 
• Transparent materials allow light to pass through them completely without scattering it. This is why we can see objects clearly through them.
 
• Some examples of transparent materials are:
 
 
• Glass
 
• Water
 
• Air
 
• Clear plastic
 
• Diamonds
 
 
 
• **Transparent materials are used in a variety of applications, such as eyeglasses, windows, lenses, and telescopes.**

• The materials are those that do not allow light to pass through them. When light strikes an opaque material, it is either absorbed or reflected. This is why we cannot see through opaque materials.
 
 
 
• **Translucent materials:-**
 
 
• These are those that allow light to pass through them, but scatter it in a way that objects behind the material are not clearly visible.
 
• This creates a unique visual effect that can be used in a wide variety of applications, from architecture to fashion.
 
 
 
• **Conductive materials:-**
 
 
• These are those that allow electricity to flow through them. This is because they have a large number of free electrons that can move around and carry the electric current.
